name: b200_8gpu_dgx

host._comment: Host side, read only by the end-to-end layer. Each figure is the conservative end of a measured or published range (disaggregation.md §1-§2, §8). root_complex: 26 GB/s is the rate measured for GPU reads from a CXL memory pool (Beluga), with about 47 GB/s in total into eight GPUs reported by Samsung; both are CXL-to-GPU measurements on other hosts, so this rate is an assumption to be calibrated per platform. pcie_link: PCIe 5.0 x16, about 63 GB/s per direction per GPU. dram: 2 TB (32 DIMMs), 218-246 GB/s summed over 16 channels (218 used), 78-114 ns (114 used). Host memory per the NVIDIA DGX B200 user guide; its drives are not described here.

_comment: NVIDIA HGX/DGX B200 8-GPU server: same Blackwell B200 chip as GB200 NVL72 (192 GB HBM3E @ 8 TB/s, FP16 dense 2250 TFLOPS/GPU per framework convention; FP8 = 4500, FP4 = 9000 by linear byte scaling), NVLink5 1.8 TB/s bidir (900 GB/s single-direction) per GPU. Single 8-GPU NVLink domain via 4 NVSwitch5 chips. B_agg = 8 × 900 GB/s = 7.2 TB/s single-dir system aggregate. Cross-node would be InfiniBand (CX7 ≈50 GB/s per port). Use this spec for production 8-GPU deployments (DGX B200 / HGX B200) instead of gb200.72gpu when modeling TP ≤ 8 — they share the same chip but differ in topology size beyond 8 GPUs. Checked against the vendor's product page in November 2026: DGX B200 lists 72 PFLOPS dense at 4-bit for 8 GPUs (9 per GPU; matches 2250 TFLOPs at 16-bit) and 1,440 GB of GPU memory (180 GB per GPU; 192 GB nominal).
